evidence_tree.built_with: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>

sources_quoted.quote: Enemy champions within {{tt|700 units|center to edge}} of you become cursed, causing them to receive {{as|12% increased magic damage|magic damage}} from all sources.

{{tip|Immobilize|Immobilizing}} an enemy champion marks them as ''Vulnerable'' for 4 seconds, increasing the damage they take from all sources by 7%. Subsequent immobilizes against a target extend the duration of the effect.

Independent damage value modifiers distinct from resistances: percentage damage amplification, percentage damage reduction, and flat damage reduction; percent modifiers stack multiplicatively with each other and with resistance-based reduction.

Sources combine by multiplying the underlying factors (10% + 10% damage reduction = 0.9 x 0.9 = 19% total reduction); applies to percent penetration, cripples, slow resist and to damage amplifiers vs damage reductions.
f(S) = the coupled participant-timeline score: deterministic total damage dealt by the main participant before its own death, summed over the fight window
m(R) = 100 / (100 + R) (apply_resistance, resistance.py) ... Resistance mitigation ... EXACT

sourced_amplifier_model.abyssal_unmake: x1.12 on MAGIC damage only, against enemy CHAMPIONS inside 700 units (S1, S2)
sourced_amplifier_model.imperial_mandate_vulnerable: x1.07 on ALL damage types, 4 s window per immobilize, refreshed/extended by subsequent immobilizes (S3)
sourced_amplifier_model.target_gate: both effects are champion-only; neither may amplify damage dealt to monsters/structures

independent_computation.reproducibility_limit: The golden scenario's participant roster, levels, ranks, loadouts and fight window live in scripts/ (golden_snapshot.py / golden_baseline.json) and in the coupled scenario definitions, all of which this runbook forbids reading and which the `data`-only export does not contain. data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json contains no scenario mentioning Abyssal Mask, Imperial Mandate, Vulnerable or a roster. An end-to-end numeric reproduction of 3072.3 is therefore not possible from the permitted evidence tree; what IS decidable from the sources is which of the two candidate values is consistent with the sourced amplifier model. That test is carried out below and it is conclusive on direction.

closed_form_exclusions.note: Let B = pre-amplifier post-mitigation team damage over the window, m = magic share of B. Any correct total must be B*(1.07 + 0.1284*m), m in [0,1]. The old and new values differ by only 1.664%, so both lie inside one feasible amp band; the question is which portion of the damage carries the 12% curse.

excluded_1.hypothesis: the change is the additive -> multiplicative composition fix (1.19 -> 1.1984 on magic)
excluded_1.arithmetic: 3022.0 * (1.1984/1.19 - 1) = 21.33, attained only if 100% of the damage were magic
excluded_1.verdict: EXCLUDED - observed delta 50.3 exceeds the maximum this fix can produce

excluded_2.hypothesis: the change newly applies the whole 7% Vulnerable amp to the team total

excluded_3.hypothesis: the change newly applies the whole 12% curse across all team damage (i.e. leaking the magic-only amp onto every damage type)
excluded_3.verdict: EXCLUDED - observed delta is 50.3; the new value does NOT over-apply the curse to non-magic damage wholesale

surviving_1.hypothesis: old under-applied: the 12% curse was absent from part/all of the roster's magic damage and the new value applies it multiplicatively per S1/S4
surviving_1.consistency: consistent; requires a roster whose magic damage is ~14% of the team total (mostly-physical roster with one magic contributor)

surviving_2.hypothesis: old used a stale 10% Abyssal constant (the pre-rework Unmake value) and the new value uses the cached-source 12% (S1/S2)
surviving_2.consistency: consistent; requires a mostly-magic roster with ~9% physical (auto attacks) - the natural shape of a scenario NAMED after the Abyssal curse

closed_form_exclusions.both_survivors_agree: Under both surviving explanations the OLD value under-states the sourced 12% magic amplification and the NEW value is the source-aligned one. No surviving explanation makes the old value the source-aligned one: making 3022.0 correct would require the new value to over-apply an amplifier, and the two wholesale over-application shapes (curse leaked onto all damage types; Vulnerable applied without an immobilize) are excluded by exclusions 2 and 3 above.

frozen_baseline_check.assessment: The frozen baseline 3269.6 sits 6.4% above the new value. No combination of the sourced constants (1.07, 1.12, 1.1984 and their magic-share blends) reproduces 3269.6 from the same base as both 3022.0 and 3072.3 under a single self-consistent rule, so the baseline is not recoverable as 'the correct value' from these two items' text alone - it reflects at least one further pre-C3 modeling difference outside this leaf's amplifier question.

verdict_basis: Directional, not a full numeric reproduction. The sourced model is unambiguous - 12% magic-only curse (S1/S2), 7% all-damage Vulnerable (S3), composed multiplicatively (S4/S5) for x1.1984 on magic and x1.07 on non-magic. The observed +50.3 (+1.664%) move is arithmetically incompatible with every wholesale over-application of these amplifiers (max 21.3 for the composition fix, 211.5 for a whole Vulnerable, 362.6 for a whole leaked curse) and is consistent only with the new value applying MORE of the sourced 12% magic amplification than the old value did. The old value is therefore the one that under-applies a cached-source amplifier.
confidence: medium-high on direction (old under-applies the sourced curse), not verified to the last decimal: the scenario roster/loadout/window needed to recompute 3072.3 end-to-end is not present in the permitted `data`-only evidence tree.
residual_risk: If the change amplified a NON-magic sub-portion of the roster's damage by 12% (a partial leak of the magic-only gate rather than a wholesale one), the delta could also be explained with the old value correct. That shape cannot be distinguished from the surviving hypotheses using data/ alone; it would require reading the per-damage-type receipt rows for this scenario, which this runbook forbids. Recommended follow-up for a non-oracle reviewer: confirm the changed amplification is gated to damage_type == magic and to champion targets.
